fullPassage: If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again. And yet, when they grew up, they might still listen to that music and play old games, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.

❌ optimistic: '낙관적인'이라는 뜻으로 반대 의미이다.
det.tip: 세 개의 수식어가 같은 방향(부정적)으로 나열되고 있음을 확인하자.

questions.passage: If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again. And yet, when they grew up, they might still listen to that music and play old games, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing <u>groundbreaking</u>. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 groundbreaking과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이것은 전혀 획기적인 것이 아니다. 이미 많은 사람들이 먼저 말하고 입증했다.
det.analysis:
✅ innovative: groundbreaking은 '획기적인, 혁신적인'이라는 의미이므로 innovative(혁신적인)가 가장 가깝다.
❌ conventional: '관습적인'이라는 뜻으로 반대 의미이다.
❌ trivial: '하찮은'이라는 뜻으로 무관한 의미이다.
❌ forgettable: '잊혀지기 쉬운'이라는 뜻으로 반대되는 느낌이다.
det.tip: ground(토대)+breaking(깨뜨리는) → 기존의 틀을 깨는 새로움이라는 어원을 떠올리자.

questions.passage:
He used to <u>play</u> video games every weekend.
The actor will <u>play</u> the leading role in the new film.
Children love to <u>play</u> tag in the park.
We <u>play</u> chess every Friday night.
questions.stem: 다음 중 밑줄 친 play의 의미가 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?

det.korean: ① 그는 주말마다 비디오 게임을 하곤 했다. ② 그 배우는 새 영화에서 주연 역을 연기할 것이다. ③ 아이들은 공원에서 태그 놀이를 하는 것을 좋아한다. ④ 우리는 금요일 밤마다 체스를 둔다.
det.analysis:
✅ He used to play video games every weekend.: '게임을 하다'라는 의미로 쓰였다.
❌ The actor will play the leading role in the new film.: '배역을 연기하다(perform a role)'라는 의미로 사용되어 나머지와 다르다.
✅ Children love to play tag in the park.: '놀이를 하다'라는 의미로 쓰였다.
✅ We play chess every Friday night.: '게임(보드게임)을 하다'라는 의미로 쓰였다.
det.tip: play는 '놀이를 하다' 외에 '배역을 연기하다', '악기를 연주하다' 등 다양한 의미가 있으므로 문맥을 확인해야 한다.

det.analysis:

❌ gratitude: '감사'라는 뜻으로 그리움의 의미와 무관하다.
det.tip: yearning for a return to the past라는 표현에서 nostalgia(향수)를 연결하자.

det.tip: more/less 뒤에는 형용사(비교급)가 와야 하므로 품사 변화를 확인하자.
